name: Drystan

attributes.attribute: Welsh hero in the Tristan and Isolt tale
wife of king March ap Meirchion who eloped with Trystan
king who negotiated a truce and set the seasonal share
chose winter but was tricked by yew trees
stays green year-round and clinched Trystan’s claim

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Trystan is a Welsh hero. A Welsh-language version tells the tale of Tristan and Isolt. The lovers are named Trystan and Esyllt. Esyllt is the wife of king March ap Meirchion. The couple eloped into a forest. March’s three armies besieged them there. King Arthur stepped in to negotiate a truce. Arthur said they must share Esyllt by season. One would have her in summer, the other in winter. March chose winter, when nights run longest. Trystan tricked him with yew trees. The yew stays green year-round. So Trystan claimed he would keep Esyllt forever. In Welsh sources the pair is called Drystan ac Esyllt. The name Drystan may derive from Pictish lore.
